To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an efficient and practical solution to the problem of ensuring data integrity in the Cloud.

1) we present a novel scheme for enabling public auditability and data dynamics in Cloud Computing; 2) we present a formal security proof for our scheme; and 3) we provide a detailed performance analysis and evaluation results.
We propose a novel approach that allows a third party auditor (TPA) to audit the cloud data without the need of the client to be involved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three main tasks.
designing a new data structure called the Merkle Hash Tree (MHT) that allows the TPA to audit data integrity without requiring any interaction with the cloud.

the design and analysis of a cryptographic scheme that allows the TPA to audit whether the data stored in the Cloud is indeed intact, while the cloud service provider does not learn the content of data stored in the client's account.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have presented a new and efficient approach for ensuring data integrity in cloud storage, which allows the client to delegate the storage of his data to a potentially malicious cloud server, and yet allows the client to audit the integrity of his data in a timely and efficient manner.
this thesis presents a novel and practical approach that enables public auditability and data dynamics for storage security in Cloud Computing.
this work presents a new approach to the problem of data storage integrity in Cloud Computing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it provides a solution for the problem of ensuring storage security in the cloud, which is based on the use of homomorphic authenticators and a new data structure that we call a Merkle-Authority-Tree (MAT).

we have developed a framework for enabling public auditability and data dynamics for storage security in cloud computing, which is a very important and necessary step towards the realization of the cloud computing paradigm.

we have designed a novel data structure called Merkle Hash Tree, which is used to verify the data integrity in the cloud storage, and also allows the client to dynamically update the data stored in the Cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that a TPA is able to perform the verification of data integrity in a public and efficient manner without requiring the client to disclose his data.
the data stored in the Cloud can be made publicly verifiable by the TPA without the need to store any extra information in the cloud.
it is indeed possible to design a system that allows the TPA to verify the integrity and freshness of the data without the need of the client to reveal his data to the TPA.
